summary: Notifications, prompts, settings, the dock, the leave flow. Graphite is the session's notification server (org.freedesktop.Notifications over QtDBus: Notify, CloseNotification, GetCapabilities, GetServerInformation, NotificationClosed, ActionInvoked) in the dedicated session (or GRAPHITE_NOTIFICATIONS=1); what apps send is shown as plain words in a toast at the foot of her column that never takes the focus (a small window of its own at the upper right while an app is in front, on X), and kept in Log (one activity-journal line each, read by Log's Events). LS_XSESSION.sh starts lxpolkit and exports its pid; session_power offers logind 'challenge' actions in the dedicated session when that agent runs. The Settings tree gains 'This computer' (Default apps, Sound, Screens, Network, Power, Session, Notifications): Default apps reads S2's catalogue and writes through the Kernel's apps.default (read back); Sound/Screens/Network/Power open S4's own pages; Session shows S1's six actions with availability (each press the System menu's own), the agent, the dock, notifications. The strip as a dock: a slim top-level window of type _NET_WM_WINDOW_TYPE_DOCK with _NET_WM_STRUT(_PARTIAL) and _NET_WM_DESKTOP all, written via ctypes/libX11 and read back, holding a 'Graphite' entry (one press brings Graphite forward, verified) and S3's strip; the in-window strip gives way to it unless Graphite is full screen. The leave flow: Log out/Restart/Shut down's confirmation names the open apps; after you confirm a dialog asks each to close politely (S3's close), shows OPEN / ASKED TO CLOSE / ASKING YOU / CANNOT BE ASKED / CLOSED with Show, and goes on once all have closed (Go on anyway, Cancel); Return to Debian in the dedicated session asks the same first. Nothing is ever killed.

decisions: The server runs only in the dedicated session (ARC_LEDGER_XSESSION=1) or with GRAPHITE_NOTIFICATIONS=1 (0 turns it off); it never takes the name from a holder (DontAllowReplacement; it says who holds it). Outside the dedicated session the desktop's own daemon keeps it.

PySide6 export: @ClassInfo D-Bus Interface + @Slot with 'uint'/'QVariantMap' types and ExportAllSlots|ExportAllSignals on a dedicated QObject that has only the spec's four methods and two signals; GetServerInformation's four outs via a QDBusMessage delayed reply with setArguments; signals as Qt Signal('uint','uint') relayed by QtDBus (clients see uint32).

Capabilities: body, actions, persistence (no body-markup: markup is stripped, text shown plain). Urgent (urgency 2) stays until closed; -1 = 8 s; 0 = never; a program's own time is held to 2..60 s. 'transient' is shown but not kept in Log (the spec's meaning). At most 20 Log lines per app per minute; the rest are counted.

Kept in Log = one activity.record line (origin DESKTOP, operation 'notification', state SHOWN) that Log's Events reads; the program's name is always quoted as given, so an app calling itself Kasandra is never read as her. No Kernel operation was added (so no registry change); notifications are data, never instructions.

Toast placement: an opaque shelf just above the right pane's foot (her column's foot, above 'ask Kasandra'), the newest nearest the foot, at most 3; when an app is in front on X, a Qt.ToolTip|WindowDoesNotAcceptFocus top-level at the upper right below the dock. Every toast widget and button has NoFocus. The default action is shown by its words as a button too.

Dock: only in the dedicated session or with GRAPHITE_DOCK=1, and only on xcb; Qt's WA_X11NetWmWindowTypeDock plus ctypes writes of type, strut, strut partial and desktop before the map, read back after (re-marked and remapped if Qt wrote another type). Graphite's window stays full screen in the dedicated session: a full-screen window covers docks while active, so S3's in-window strip still shows then; when Graphite is not full screen it sits below the dock and its own strip gives way (room() 0). The dock raises itself when another window becomes active (harmless under a dock-aware manager; needed under the stand-in).

Leave flow order (nothing stopped before you confirm): availability, your work questions, the confirmation (now naming open apps), the apps dialog (asks politely, waits; Show, Ask again, Go on anyway, Cancel), Graphite's ordinary close, the system's command. Return to Debian (dedicated session only) runs the apps step before the return-copy review; an app already closed stays closed if you then continue working. Only main windows are asked to close; an app's own dialog ('Save changes?') shows as ASKING YOU and is answered in the app.

polkit_agent: the session's ARC_LEDGER_POLKIT_AGENT_PID checked against /proc comm (lxpolkit and other known agents, same uid); a /proc scan only when reading Graphite's own environment, so an explicit environment (as in the tests) is answered from itself alone. NO_PROMPT's words are unchanged (test_system_menu's assertions still hold by reading); the agent's words are appended.

Settings: a 'This computer' root above Workspace and Assistant; Sound/Screens/Network/Power open S4's MachineRoom (S4's functions) and the left pane stays on Settings when you came from there; Default apps reads apps_catalog directly and writes through the Kernel's apps.default (approve scope, read back); a web address sets http and https together. On-screen words say 'apps', never 'programs'.
findings_for_the_coordinator: notify-send is not installed here: the 'notify-send-shaped' calls were made with gdbus call in notify-send's argument shape (app 'notify-send', replaces 0, '', summary, body, [], {urgency byte, sender-pid int64}, -1).

Fluxbox's dock layer and strut handling were not seen: the Xvfb run used S3's stand-in EWMH manager, which reads no strut and raises activated windows (the smoke placed Graphite below the dock by hand, as a strut-aware manager would). The dock's properties were read back from the X server.
lxpolkit was not run (not installed): a stand-in binary named lxpolkit and stub scripts were used. R1's package set must carry lxpolkit (it is in the plan's list).

Merge points: shell2.py hunk right after install_her_column (P1); settings_qt SettingsNavigator.__init__ node loop and selected(); navigation_qt follow() (S4's MachineRoom line became a block); windows_strip_qt.room; session_power availability/confirm/run_action/leave; context_menu settings_entries; tail_words after QUIET_ORIGINS; workspace_tabs open_record before ComputerTab. No registry or seed change.
P2 (Day look) was not in this tree: no Day frames; the toasts, dock and pages use boss_theme tokens only, so they should follow the Day palette.

tests_integrated/test_context_menu.py (about line 472) right-clicks the Settings tree's first child, now 'Default apps' under This computer instead of a Workspace group; its assertions (kind 'setting'; expand, collapse, search offered) still hold by reading, not run.
Offscreen, QDialog.adjustSize prints 'This plugin does not support propagateSizeHints()' (harmless; the only stderr lines).
not_done: Nothing was tested in the owner's sense, and nothing ran on the ThinkPad, under Fluxbox, with real lxpolkit, real libnotify clients or a real polkit prompt.
No Day-look frames (P2 not in this tree).
Notification icons and image-data are not shown (a kind mark and words instead); no sound; no quiet hours beyond 'Only keep them in Log'.
Kasandra does not read notifications (no Kernel observation registered); K2 could read notify_server.Notes.recent().
The dock covers the primary screen's top edge only; no per-screen docks.
Closing Graphite's window by other routes (its own close in the dedicated session) does not run the apps step; the System menu's and File menu's leave and power rows do.
release_note: Notifications, prompts and settings: Graphite is now the session's notification server, so messages from your apps appear quietly at the foot of Kasandra's column (never taking the keyboard) and are kept in Log; the session starts a permission agent so the system's own password prompts can be answered; Settings > This computer reaches default apps, sound, screens, network, power, the session and notifications; the window strip also stands in a slim dock above every app, with a Graphite entry that always brings Graphite back; and before Log out, Restart, Shut down or Return to Debian, Graphite names the apps still open and asks them to close politely first. Built, not tested on the ThinkPad.
